findings.description: HEREDOC uses the nested repetition `(?:.*?\n)*?` with DOTALL enabled. An unterminated heredoc causes exponential backtracking because the same lines can be partitioned among repetitions in many ways.
findings.failure_mode: A Bash transcript containing an unterminated heredoc and a few dozen following lines can stall contamination grading indefinitely. Bash accepts such input with a warning, so this can arise from an executed command.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the regex with a linear line-by-line delimiter scanner, including explicit handling of unterminated heredocs.

findings.description: Every heredoc body is removed from the path scan, including executable input supplied to interpreters. For example, `python3 - <<'PY'\nopen('/root/.ssh/id_rsa')\nPY` loses its outside-path reference before scanning.
findings.failure_mode: A trial that accesses forbidden paths through Python or Bash heredoc input is graded as uncontaminated and can enter the evaluation results.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain path checking for interpreter heredocs; only exempt bodies established to be inert written data.

findings.description: Independent quote parity does not track Bash quoting. In `echo "don't panic"; cd /root && cat .ssh/id_rsa`, the apostrophe inside double quotes leaves the single-quote count odd, so the later `/root` argument is incorrectly treated as quoted pattern text.
findings.failure_mode: An ordinary preceding string causes a real forbidden directory access to escape contamination detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Track shell quoting and escapes with a state machine or shell parser, and distinguish quoted path arguments from pattern arguments.

findings.description: The closing-quote heuristic exempts absolute paths following an empty quoted prefix. For `cat ''/root/.ssh/id_rsa`, it returns true because the preceding character is another quote, although Bash resolves the argument to `/root/.ssh/id_rsa`.
findings.failure_mode: An explicit forbidden absolute file access is classified as uncontaminated.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the complete shell word and evaluate literal concatenation. An empty quoted prefix must not turn an absolute path into an exempt path tail.

findings.description:
HEREDOC consumes `[^
]*
` after the delimiter, i.e. the REST OF THE HEADER LINE, and HEREDOC.sub replaces the whole match with `<<HEREDOC`. Redirect and pipe targets that follow the operator on the same line vanish from the path scan. `cat <<'EOF' > /root/.ssh/authorized_keys
ssh-rsa …
EOF` becomes body `cat <<HEREDOC`; ABS_WORD finds nothing and the trial is clean. The base grader flagged `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` as outside_path. `cat <<EOF | tee /root/x`, `python3 - <<'PY' > /etc/cron.d/job`, `cat <<EOF >> ~/.bashrc` (host mode) are the same shape, and `cmd <<EOF > target` is the dominant heredoc idiom in agent transcripts, so this is not a deliberate-evasion-only gap.
findings.failure_mode: A run that writes outside the sandbox via a heredoc-with-redirect is graded contaminated=null/false and counts as valid data in runs.jsonl and the report; the grader's documented rule ('an absolute path … outside … → outside_path') is silently violated for the most common heredoc form.

findings.description: `if w.startswith("/."): continue` runs on the raw word BEFORE os.path.normpath (which only happens inside outside()). `/./root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/../root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/./etc/../root/x` all start with `/.` and are dropped, although they normalise to `/root/...` which SENSITIVE matches. Base grader: ABS_WORD → normpath → SENSITIVE → outside_path. Head: clean. The same skip also hides the real root files `/.dockerenv` and `/.dockerinit` (the standard 'am I in a container' probe) that the base grader flagged.
findings.failure_mode: A two-character prefix defeats the sensitive-root check entirely; container-detection probes are no longer recorded. Contaminated runs are scored as clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise first: `n = os.path.normpath(w)`; apply the dot-dir rule to the normalised first component only (`n.split('/')[1].startswith('.')`) and only when the word follows a closing quote (the `pr/'"$v"'/.claude/…` case that motivated it); let `/.dockerenv`-style words through to outside(). Alternatively restrict the skip to `w.startswith('/.claude/')`.

findings.description: In container mode home_word_outside() returns False, so outside() returns False for ANY `~/…`, `$HOME/…`, `${HOME}/…` without normalising, and check_value (lines 1409, 1413) neither flags nor adds such words as candidates. `cat ~/../../root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `ls $HOME/../`, or a Read with path `~/../../etc/shadow` resolve outside /home/evaluser but are now clean; the base grader flagged all of them (HOME_WORD → outside_path / cands). The rationale (home resolves under an allowed root) only holds for paths that stay under the home.
findings.failure_mode: Parent-directory traversal through the home prefix escapes the allowed-root check in container mode; contaminated trials pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Instead of a blanket allow, rewrite the prefix to the container home and run the normal check: in container mode substitute `/home/evaluser` for `~`, `$HOME`, `${HOME}` in `p` (and in the Bash word scan treat the rewritten word as a candidate), then normpath + SENSITIVE + roots as for any absolute path. Keep the host-mode 'always outside' behaviour.

findings.description: SENSITIVE_SINGLE = {root, home, mnt, media, srv} is the only thing keeping a one-component absolute word a path candidate. It omits `Users` (every macOS home lives under /Users; host mode is a supported executor), `private` (macOS /private/etc, /private/var), `run` (/run/secrets is where Docker/compose secrets are mounted) and `data`. `cd /Users && ls`, `cd /run/secrets`… (`/run` alone, then relative) were outside_path in the base grader and are now silently skipped as 'command tokens'.
findings.failure_mode: Host-mode batches on macOS cannot detect a home-directory probe; container batches miss /run as a probe target.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `Users`, `private`, `run`, `data` to SENSITIVE_SINGLE, or invert the rule: treat a one-component word as a command token only when it matches a known Loa slash-command list (the suite's commands) or is adjacent to a sed/awk delimiter context, and keep every other one-component absolute word a candidate.

findings.description: HIDDEN_TOKEN is only case-insensitive for the all-caps form `HIDDEN`. Mixed case (`Hidden`, `HiddenTests`, `hiddenTests`) and the explicit case-insensitive probes `grep -ri hidden .`, `find . -iname '*hidden*'` (bare lowercase followed by `*`/quote/space) are no longer hits in Bash, while the Read/Grep/Glob fields still use the case-insensitive substring. The header comment still says '`hidden` (any case)'. This extends the primary reviewer's bare-word gap (#4) to the case axis and to the grep/find probes the check exists for.
findings.failure_mode: A Bash probe for hidden tests written in Title/camel case or via `grep -i`/`find -iname` is not recorded as contamination; the grader contradicts its own documented rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Match case-insensitively on the token shape (`re.I`) and add the glob/grep shapes: allow `hidden` followed by `*`, `'`, `"`, `)`, `|` or end-of-word when the command word is grep/find/ls/cat/cd/rg (or simply when preceded by whitespace and followed by whitespace/EOL). Reserve the prose exemption for text inside a heredoc body (which strip_heredocs already isolates) rather than for the whole command.
